analysis: What changed versus the 5 AM PT brief: September CPI hit the wire at 5:30 AM PT and repriced the morning in minutes. Headline matched at 3.7% y/y (+0.6% m/m), but core came in 2.6% y/y versus 2.5% expected — the one decimal point that mattered. The pre-CPI futures tape (Dow +0.45%, S&P +0.21%, Nasdaq flat) flipped red (Nasdaq-100 -0.5%, S&P -0.2%, Dow -0.1%), the 10Y jumped to 5.26% from 5.19% pre-reading, and October hike odds nearly doubled from ~22% to ~39%. The bank-wave winners and losers from the 4/5 AM briefs kept their premarket direction (BLK now +5%, BAC now -5%), which reads as the tape separating earnings from rates: bank stock moves are about their prints, while the index is about the Fed. Memory stays the fragile corner — U.S. names keep bleeding on a CXMT claim that is still unconfirmed, and this morning the pushback gained analysts' names: Jefferies says it is not clear the tech is commercial, Morningstar expects a meaningful gap to viable yields. Earnings context carried: BAC Q3 adjusted EPS $1.08 vs $1.10 consensus on a $1.2B AML fine; MS Q3 EPS $3.03 vs $2.93; BLK adjusted EPS $15.93 vs $14.32 with $15.49T AUM. Signal vs noise: the CPI numbers are confirmed via IBD and Investopedia live coverage (and line up with the BLS 8:30 AM ET release); bank prints confirmed via WSJ/IBD; the CXMT 4F2 claim rests on the company's own conference remarks with no independent verification — the memory selloff is fragile by definition. Community channels were quiet — one 2-point HN thread on the CPI number itself, nothing on Reddit that qualified.

headlines.headline: September CPI (released 5:30 AM PT): headline +0.6% m/m and 3.7% y/y (matching consensus, up from 3.4% in August); core +0.3% m/m and 2.6% y/y — hotter than the 2.5% consensus. Post-print: Nasdaq-100 futures -0.5%, S&P 500 futures -0.2%, Dow futures -0.1%; 10Y Treasury jumped to 5.26% from 5.19% pre-reading (Tuesday close 5.22%); October Fed hike odds rose to ~39% from ~22% (CME FedWatch).
headlines.why_it_matters: Headline matched but core missed by a tenth — that is the part the Fed watches, so the whole rate curve repriced within minutes: higher yields, lower futures, and a near-doubling of October hike odds.

headlines.headline: Bank of America now -4% to -5% premarket after reporting adjusted EPS $1.08 vs $1.10 consensus on $30.12B revenue vs $30.6B expected, alongside the $1.2B Treasury AML fine. BlackRock +5% (adjusted EPS $15.93 vs $14.32, $15.49T AUM on $205B inflows); Morgan Stanley up less than 1% (EPS $3.03 vs $2.93, equities revenue +41%). State Street still sliding toward a three-month low on its mixed print.
headlines.why_it_matters: Premarket directions from the 4/5 AM briefs held through the CPI print — BAC is being priced on governance and the miss, BLK on a clean beat — which means the earnings wave is trading on its own merits while the index trades on the Fed.

headlines.headline: Memory selloff extends: CXMT's claim of a 4F2 DRAM breakthrough (DDR5 server RDIMMs before year-end) still has no independent verification; Jefferies says it is 'not clear if this technology is commercial' and Morningstar expects a 'meaningful time gap' between the unveiling and commercialization at viable yields. Samsung and SK Hynix each fell over 7% Tuesday on the claim; KOSPI fell 6%, its steepest single-day decline since July; Micron closed -4% Monday and keeps bleeding premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: The claim is still single-source — treat the whole memory selloff as fragile. But named-analyst skepticism (Jefferies, Morningstar) is now on record, which gives dip-buyers cover and sets up a violent reversal if the claim gets debunked or confirmed.

headlines.headline: Crude stays the inflation tail-risk: WTI rallied to ~$95.35 (+>1%) and Brent pushed above $106 as Saudi/Houthi fighting escalates; China's September imports +31.0% y/y vs +24.5% expected. Gold futures ~$4,160; bitcoin slipped to ~$82,700 post-CPI.
headlines.why_it_matters: Energy inflation at these levels is exactly what keeps a hawkish Fed alive — the next leg of the CPI debate will be driven as much by crude as by core.
